parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The gravitational field strength $g$ at a distance $x$ from the centre of a uniform spherical planet of mass $M$ is given by the expression $$g = \frac{GM}{x^2}$$ where $G$ is the gravitational constant and distance $x$ is greater than the radius of the planet.
parts.text: Describe the pattern of the field lines outside the planet that represent the gravitational field due to the planet.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why, for small changes in vertical height near the surface of the planet, $g$ may be assumed to be constant.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Assume that the Earth is a uniform sphere. For the Earth, the product $GM$ is equal to $3.99 \times 10^{14} \text{m}^3 \text{s}^{-2}$.
parts.text: Determine a value, to three significant figures, for the radius $R$ of the Earth.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the gravitational potential at the Earth's surface. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why the gravitational potential energy of two point masses is always negative.
